bullets: Labor markets are where macro stops being abstract — the point at which economic conditions become concrete realities for workers and households rather than aggregate figures.
Risk is a household-level variable rather than a portfolio-level one; a pattern observed to hold consistently across three different teams.
Ignoring the household and labor-market grounding of risk forces teams to rebuild their approach from scratch a year later — a recurring pattern at teams using Bloomberg and BloombergNEF.
Systems thinking involves trade-offs that cross-cut every other theme, from labor markets to risk management, rather than standing as a separate topic.
Adoption works best by picking one idea and running it for two weeks rather than overhauling everything at once — the rest is iteration.
